cards.text: Jesus has just finished talking to the crowds about John the Baptist (Matthew 11:7-19). Now He turns to the cities where most of His miracles were performed, and He begins to denounce them. Friend, this is NOT a thank-you speech.

cards.question: Jesus denounces the cities that saw most of His miracles. What's the reason?

cards.text: Jesus starts with two towns: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!" Two woes, back to back, like waking up to two missed calls from your boss before 8 a.m.

cards.question: Jesus says if the miracles done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, what would those cities have done?
Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Chorazin and Bethsaida than for Tyre and Sidon.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to Capernaum, the town He went to live in (Matthew 4:13). Talk about getting called out in your OWN neighborhood group chat.

cards.question: Jesus asks Capernaum if it will be lifted up to heaven. No, He says, it will be brought down to ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up Sodom, the city the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24). Friend, when THAT'S the city you're being compared to, the meeting is not going well.

cards.question: If the miracles done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, what does Jesus say would have happened to Sodom?

answers.text: It would have remained to this day
It would have been destroyed sooner
It would have mocked Him just the same

cards.question: Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Sodom than for Capernaum.

cards.text: Then the whole tone changes. Jesus declares, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth," and He tells the Father why.

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned. Who does the Father reveal them to?

cards.text: Jesus adds, "Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight." Then He says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father. Friend, nobody knows ME like that. The dead batteries I shared that drawer with spent five years calling me "the mustache guy."

cards.question: Jesus says no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

cards.text: And now, after all those woes, comes an invitation: "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened," Jesus says. Friend, that "all" covers everybody who has ever hit snooze FOUR times and then argued with the alarm.

cards.question: Jesus invites everyone who is weary and burdened to come to Him, and He promises to give them ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart." Friend, I spent years under a pile of old takeout menus in a junk drawer, so a gentle and humble teacher? I am SO in.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever takes His yoke and learns from Him will find ___ for their souls.
Jesus ends by telling why His yoke brings rest. How does He describe His yoke and His burden?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences and more than two beats: the verse 26 quote, all things entrusted to the Son, no one knows the Son except the Father, and then a two-sentence joke. Split it, or cut it down to 1 to 2 sentences with no more than two beats.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has more than two things happening (Matthew 11:26, the first claim of 11:27, the second claim of 11:27, plus the joke).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke adds new facts to Papa Dorin's backstory. It gives an exact time in the drawer ("five years") and a made-up drawer moment (the batteries calling him "the mustache guy"). The backstory only says "years." Made-up moments are allowed only around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "Friend, nobody knows ME like that" puts Papa Dorin's joke right next to the Father's unique knowledge of the Son. Read as a comparison, it lands the laugh on Jesus' words about the Father and the Son rather than on Papa Dorin's own situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the core action of the verse, which is taking a yoke and learning from a gentle, humble teacher. Lying under takeout menus in a drawer has no clear link to wanting a gentle teacher, so a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Tyre and Sidon, and also Chorazin and Bethsaida, show up with no word on who or what they are. Capernaum (card 6) and Sodom (card 8) do get a short introduction. The "New people" rule speaks of "someone," so it's unclear whether it covers cities.
findings.question: Does the "New people" rule (say simply who they are the first time they show up) also apply to places like cities, so Tyre and Sidon would need a short introduction, such as coastal cities outside Israel?
